purpose: Reach a rule-driven stop on live data. The three earlier runs all stopped on a screening budget, so the recall rule never had a second population estimate and could not fire. This run was sized so several iterations fit inside a comparable budget.

design.seed_criterion: 5-35 references and >=10 citations, from the 260-record innovation x marketing x automation corpus, so iteration 1 stays small
design.direction_rationale: forward expansion produced 2-10x more candidates than backward in every earlier run and is unbounded for a well-cited paper
design.budget_rationale: deliberately non-binding, so whatever fires is a saturation rule rather than a budget

status: COMPLETE — stopped by the exhaustion rule after 10 iterations.

result_so_far.note: The paper's central claim, measured outside simulation. At iteration 1 the estimator reported a population of 6.0 against 6 observed — recall 1.000 with the lower bound also at 1.000, i.e. apparently complete. The population then climbed to 43.7, 132.5, 285.5, 534.1, 629.6, 638.5, 642.1 and settled at 643.3. The iteration-1 estimate was wrong by a factor of 107, and wrong in the direction that matters: an unguarded rule would have terminated the review after six included studies out of 591.
result_so_far.guard_behaviour: Correct at every iteration: the lower CI bound reached 0.942 and 0.930, below tau=0.95, and N_hat drift of +629% and +203% is far outside the 5% stability requirement, so the rule withheld on both grounds.
result_so_far.what_releases_the_rule: The lower confidence bound has flattened at 0.930-0.932 rather than climbing toward the 0.95 threshold, because the estimated population grows in step with the observed count. The threshold condition is therefore not what will release this rule — the stability condition is. Drift is decelerating monotonically (+629%, +203%, +115%) but is still an order of magnitude outside the 5% band.
result_so_far.what_happened_to_the_recall_rule: It never fired, and correctly so. The lower confidence bound fell from 1.000 to a plateau at 0.877 as the estimated population grew faster than the observed count, so the 0.95 threshold was never met after iteration 1. The stability condition was eventually satisfied — drift fell to 1.4%, then 0.6%, then 0.2% — but the threshold condition was not. The rule that did fire was exhaustion, and the run's own recall estimate says why that was the right outcome: at 0.908 estimated recall there was still literature to find, so no early stop was warranted.

how_to_finish.step1: screen /tmp/narrow_cand4.json with validation/llm_screen_validate.py (two-stage gate, the protocol validated in supplementary Section S2), writing labels_narrow_004.csv
how_to_finish.step3: repeat until stopped_by is 'estimated_recall' or 'marginal_yield' rather than 'budget'
how_to_finish.expectation: marginal yield fell 11.2% -> 5.2% between iterations 2 and 3 and its threshold is 2%, so on the present trend it is the rule most likely to fire first, probably within two or three further iterations.

result.rationale: Citation searching was continued until the frontier was exhausted after iteration 10: no newly included study remained whose references and citations had not already been retrieved.
result.note: This is the first of the four live runs to terminate on a saturation criterion rather than on a resource limit. The budget of 20,000 was never reached; the run stopped because the citation graph reachable from the seeds was closed.
